title: Do you share too much online
paragraphs: It’s good to share, right? Growing up as kids we are told to share our toys and not be selfish. We also live in an age where discussing our feelings is encouraged. But when does it all become too much? With new crazes trending all the time, such as dance challenges and wearing a pillow as a dress, the question is: when can sharing become oversharing on social media?

What is oversharing? The term has become associated with social media, but it isn’t exclusive to this platform. Imagine you head to a party and you meet someone. Within five minutes they have divulged intimate details about their life. While some of us may try to escape these people, according to marriage therapist Carolyn Cole, this form of oversharing could come from a strong desire to connect with someone. But how does this translate to social media?

Dr Christopher Hand, a lecturer in cyberpsychology, says the more details people disclose, the less sympathy we express when things go wrong. This could be due to a belief that we attract our own negative experiences the more we share them. It seems that sadfishing, the idea of searching for sympathy by oversharing, is generally perceived as negative rather than the cry for help it could actually be. However, Dr Hand’s research also seems to suggest that the more we post on a platform, the more socially attractive we become – provided that the posts we bang out are positive. Even back in 2015, Gwendolyn Seidman PhD, said that we should avoiding whining and being negative online. We should also steer clear of showing off, bragging or flexing, as it’s now known – especially about our love lives. It makes sense – if your date is going ‘that well’, would you really have time to share a photo with text?

So, how can you know if you are oversharing? Well, why not ask your friends in real life. They would probably be more than happy to tell you if your posts about your breakfast or your gripes about your lack of money really are too much.

vocabulary.entry: craze /kreɪz/ n. 狂热；风靡一时的事物
vocabulary.example: The new fitness craze has swept the whole country.
vocabulary.translation: 这种新的健身热潮席卷了全国。

vocabulary.entry: trend /trend/ v. 流行；成为趋势
vocabulary.example: Minimalist designs are trending this season.
vocabulary.translation: 极简风格本季正流行。

vocabulary.example: Oversharing personal information online can be risky.
vocabulary.translation: 在网上过度分享个人信息可能有风险。

vocabulary.entry: social media /ˈsəʊʃl ˈmiːdiə/ n. 社交媒体
vocabulary.example: She spends too much time on social media every day.
vocabulary.translation: 她每天花太多时间在社交媒体上。

vocabulary.example: He refused to divulge any details about the project.
vocabulary.translation: 他拒绝透露该项目的任何细节。

vocabulary.entry: intimate detail /ˈɪntɪmət dɪˈteɪl/ n. 私密细节
vocabulary.example: She doesn't like to talk about intimate details of her life.
vocabulary.translation: 她不喜欢谈论自己生活的私密细节。

vocabulary.entry: connect with /kəˈnekt wɪð/ 与……建立联系
vocabulary.example: The teacher tries to connect with every student in the class.
vocabulary.translation: 这位老师努力和班上的每个学生建立联系。

vocabulary.example: Cyberpsychology studies how people behave online.
vocabulary.translation: 网络心理学研究人们在网络上的行为。

vocabulary.example: The company refused to disclose its financial data.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司拒绝披露其财务数据。

vocabulary.example: She expressed her sympathy for the victims of the accident.
vocabulary.translation: 她对事故受害者表示了同情。

vocabulary.entry: negative experience /ˈneɡətɪv ɪkˈspɪəriəns/ n. 负面经历
vocabulary.example: The negative experience made her afraid to try again.
vocabulary.translation: 那次负面经历让她不敢再尝试了。

vocabulary.example: Sadfishing online may not get the sympathy people want.
vocabulary.translation: 在网上卖惨式分享可能得不到人们想要的同情。

vocabulary.example: She is perceived as a very reliable colleague.
vocabulary.translation: 她被认为是个非常可靠的同事。

vocabulary.entry: socially attractive /ˈsəʊʃəli əˈtræktɪv/ adj. 有社交吸引力的
vocabulary.example: People with a sense of humor are often socially attractive.
vocabulary.translation: 有幽默感的人往往很有社交吸引力。

vocabulary.entry: bang out /bæŋ aʊt/ 快速发布；匆匆写出
vocabulary.example: He banged out three posts on his blog in one hour.
vocabulary.translation: 他一小时内就在自己的博客上快速发布了三篇帖子。

vocabulary.example: Stop whining about the cold and put on a jacket.
vocabulary.translation: 别抱怨天冷了，穿上外套吧。

vocabulary.entry: steer clear of /stɪə klɪə ɒv/ 避开；远离
vocabulary.example: You should steer clear of him; he's always in trouble.
vocabulary.translation: 你应该离他远点，他总是惹麻烦。

vocabulary.entry: show off /ʃəʊ ɒf/ 炫耀；卖弄
vocabulary.example: He likes to show off his new car to his friends.
vocabulary.translation: 他喜欢向朋友们炫耀自己的新车。

vocabulary.example: She is always bragging about her children's achievements.
vocabulary.translation: 她总是吹嘘自己孩子的成就。

vocabulary.example: He likes to flex his wealth on social media.
vocabulary.translation: 他喜欢在社交媒体上炫耀自己的财富。

vocabulary.example: His main gripe is that he doesn't get enough paid leave.
vocabulary.translation: 他最大的抱怨是带薪休假不够多。

sentences.english: What is oversharing?
sentences.chinese: 什么是过度分享？

sentences.chinese: 这个说法如今常和社交媒体挂钩，但并非仅限于这一平台。

sentences.chinese: 短短五分钟内，对方就把自己的私密生活细节和盘托出。

sentences.english: While some of us may try to escape these people, according to marriage therapist Carolyn Cole, this form of oversharing could come from a strong desire to connect with someone.
sentences.chinese: 虽然我们有些人可能会想方设法躲开这类人，但婚姻治疗师卡罗琳·科尔表示，这种过度分享的行为，可能源于一种想要与人建立联结的强烈渴望。

sentences.english: But how does this translate to social media?
sentences.chinese: 但这种行为放到社交媒体上，又会是怎样的情况呢？

sentences.chinese: 网络心理学讲师克里斯托弗·汉德博士表示，人们披露的个人细节越多，当他们遭遇不顺时，我们给予的同情就越少。

sentences.chinese: 这可能是因为人们认为，分享负面经历的次数越多，就越容易招致更多不顺。

sentences.chinese: “卖惨式分享”指的是通过过度分享来博取同情，这种行为通常被认为是负面的，而不是一种真实的求助信号。

sentences.english: However, Dr Hand’s research also seems to suggest that the more we post on a platform, the more socially attractive we become – provided that the posts we bang out are positive.
sentences.chinese: 不过汉德博士的研究也表明，只要我们发布的内容都是积极向上的，在社交平台上发帖越频繁，我们的社交吸引力就越强。

sentences.english: Even back in 2015, Gwendolyn Seidman PhD, said that we should avoiding whining and being negative online.
sentences.chinese: 早在2015年，格温多琳·塞德曼博士就曾说过，我们应该避免在网上抱怨和传播负面情绪。

sentences.english: We should also steer clear of showing off, bragging or flexing, as it’s now known – especially about our love lives.
sentences.chinese: 我们还应避免炫耀、吹嘘或如今所说的“晒优越”——尤其是在感情生活方面。

sentences.english: It makes sense – if your date is going ‘that well’, would you really have time to share a photo with text?
sentences.chinese: 这其实很容易理解——如果你的约会进展得“那么顺利”，你真的会有时间发图文分享吗？

sentences.english: So, how can you know if you are oversharing?
sentences.chinese: 那么，怎样才能判断自己是否过度分享了呢？

sentences.english: Well, why not ask your friends in real life.
sentences.chinese: 不妨问问你现实生活中的朋友。

sentences.english: They would probably be more than happy to tell you if your posts about your breakfast or your gripes about your lack of money really are too much.
sentences.chinese: 如果你发的早餐照片，或是吐槽自己缺钱的帖子实在太过了，他们很可能会乐意告诉你。
